purpose: Phase D -- chunk1 (surviving worker, PID 20471) as live evidence for whether a single worker is bounded, distinct from the killed chunk0.

samples.note: chunk0 (PID 20454) OOM-killed at 12109308kB anon-rss THIS MOMENT -- chunk1 unaffected, kept running
first post-incident sample -- chunk1 alone, briefly higher (had more headroom to expand into once chunk0's memory was freed)
calibration worker (PID 24075) launched around this time, cold-starting

interpretation.while_concurrent_with_chunk0: range 6.58-9.83GB across 6 samples, 18-29 pages -- itself never approached 12GB, but was contributing to the TOTAL system pressure that killed chunk0 (chunk0 alone reached 12.1GB; the two together exceeded 31GB with 0 swap).
interpretation.after_chunk0_died_alone: range 8.25-10.87GB across 8 samples, 29 pages -> still processing -- a SLIGHTLY WIDER but not qualitatively different band than while concurrent. Critically: NOT trending toward 12GB+ over this window (14 min, no page-count delta captured for the alone period specifically since chunk1's own page count wasn't re-sampled every check, but the process has stayed alive and productive throughout).
interpretation.even_with_a_second_process_now_running_c: chunk1 remained in the SAME 8.4-9.7GB band while the calibration worker (PID 24075) ran alongside it and itself spiked to 5.3GB mid-page -- i.e. chunk1 did not show any coupling/amplification effect from a second small/short-lived process being present.
interpretation.conclusion_so_far: SUPPORTS Phase D's stated hypothesis: 'concurrency amplifies peak RAM, but a single worker may be viable.' chunk1 alone has NOT shown sustained growth toward the 12GB+ danger zone across 14 samples spanning ~30 minutes and both solo and multi-process conditions. This is not yet proof a single worker can NEVER reach 12GB (chunk0 itself lived through 32 pages before its fatal spike, so a longer observation window is warranted before fully closing this question) -- but it is real, multi-point, non-cherry-picked evidence in favor of Mode 1/2 recovery being safe, not merely an assumption.
interpretation.caveat: chunk0 also looked bounded for its first 32 pages before dying on page 33 (in-flight) -- this timeline does not yet rule out a rare, late-onset large spike. The Phase F calibration test (in progress) adds independent evidence from a FRESH, isolated process rather than extrapolating from chunk1's long-lived one.
